rmt-2009-gen-01.title: Positions at the end
rmt-2009-gen-01.body:
The train travels $10\cdot20=200$ m before stopping, so after $35$ s MacGyver is $400+200=600$ m from where the raptors started. The raptors are then $5$ m behind him, so they ran $595$ m in $35$ s: $v=\frac{595}{35}=17$ m/s.

**Answer: 17 m/s**

rmt-2009-gen-01.title: Gap closing
rmt-2009-gen-01.body:
The gap starts at $400$ m. During the first $20$ s it shrinks at rate $v-10$, then for the next $15$ s at rate $v$. The final gap is $5$: $400-20(v-10)-15v=5$, so $600-35v=5$ and $v=17$.

**Answer: 17 m/s**

rmt-2009-gen-02.title: Sectors around the barn
rmt-2009-gen-02.body:
Around the corner where he is tied, Earl can sweep a $270^\circ$ sector of radius $20$: area $\frac34\pi\cdot20^2=300\pi$. Going around either adjacent corner, $10$ of the leash is used along the wall, leaving length $10$, which sweeps a quarter circle of radius $10$ beyond each of those corners: $2\cdot\frac14\pi\cdot10^2=50\pi$. (The remaining leash after going around two corners is $0$, so nothing more is reachable.) Total $350\pi$.

**Answer: $350\pi$**

rmt-2009-gen-02.title: Check the pieces
rmt-2009-gen-02.body:
Total area $=\frac{3}{4}\cdot400\pi+\frac12\cdot100\pi=300\pi+50\pi=350\pi\approx1099.6$ square units. The two quarter circles of radius $10$ together make half a disk of radius $10$.

**Answer: $350\pi$**

rmt-2009-gen-03.title: Vertex of a parabola
rmt-2009-gen-03.body:
Area $=(2x+15)(10-x)=-2x^2+5x+150$, a downward parabola with maximum at $x=-\frac{b}{2a}=\frac{5}{4}$.

**Answer: $\frac54$**

rmt-2009-gen-03.title: Symmetry of the roots
rmt-2009-gen-03.body:
The area is zero at $x=-\frac{15}2$ and $x=10$; the maximum is at the midpoint $\frac{-7.5+10}2=\frac54$.

**Answer: $\frac54$**

rmt-2009-gen-05.title: Consecutive angles are supplementary
rmt-2009-gen-05.body:
The two different angles of a parallelogram add to $180^\circ$. If the smaller is $x$, then $x+4x=180^\circ$, so $x=36^\circ$ and the larger angle is $144^\circ$.

**Answer: $144^\circ$**

rmt-2009-gen-06.title: Marginal analysis
rmt-2009-gen-06.body:
Each upgrade saves $0.10\cdot10001=1000.10$ dollars on the fizzbangs. The $k$th upgrade costs $100k$ dollars, so it pays off while $100k<1000.1$, i.e. for $k\le10$. With $10$ upgrades the unit cost is $1$ dollar: fizzbangs cost $10001$ and upgrades cost $100(1+2+\dots+10)=5500$. Total $15501$.

An $11$th upgrade would cost $1100>1000.1$ in savings, so it does not help.

**Answer: 15501 dollars**

rmt-2009-gen-07.title: Find the intersection points
rmt-2009-gen-07.body:
A point on $y=10-x$ at distance $\sqrt{82}$ from the origin satisfies $x^2+(10-x)^2=82$, i.e. $x^2-10x+9=0$, so $x=1$ or $9$: the points $(1,9)$ and $(9,1)$. The slopes of the lines from the origin are $m=9$ and $m=\frac19$, with product $1$.

**Answer: 1**

rmt-2009-gen-07.title: Reflection symmetry
rmt-2009-gen-07.body:
If $(x,y)$ is such a point, so is $(y,x)$ (same distance, still on $x+y=10$). The slopes of the lines through the origin are $\frac yx$ and $\frac xy$, whose product is $1$.

**Answer: 1**

rmt-2009-gen-08.title: Least common multiple
rmt-2009-gen-08.body:
If he bakes $t$ tarts, he uses $\frac t4$, $\frac t7$, $\frac t{10}$ containers of the three berries, and these must be whole numbers of containers. So $t$ is a multiple of $\operatorname{lcm}(4,7,10)=140$. The smallest case $t=140$ uses $35+20+14=69$ containers.

**Answer: 69 containers**

rmt-2009-gen-09.title: Similar cones
rmt-2009-gen-09.body:
The melted ice cream fills a small cone (point down) of height $3$ similar to the whole cone, so its radius is $\frac38\cdot5=\frac{15}8$. Its volume is $\frac13\pi\left(\frac{15}8\right)^2\cdot3=\frac{225\pi}{64}$.

**Answer: $\frac{225\pi}{64}$**

rmt-2009-gen-09.title: Volume scales as the cube
rmt-2009-gen-09.body:
The full cone has volume $\frac13\pi\cdot25\cdot8=\frac{200\pi}3$. The small cone is similar with ratio $\frac38$, so its volume is $\frac{200\pi}3\cdot\frac{27}{512}=\frac{225\pi}{64}$.

**Answer: $\frac{225\pi}{64}$**

rmt-2009-gen-10.title: Equation
rmt-2009-gen-10.body:
Let $x$ be the length without windows. Then $120x+80(20-x)=2120$, so $40x=520$ and $x=13$.

**Answer: 13 meters**

rmt-2009-gen-10.title: All windows first
rmt-2009-gen-10.body:
If the whole wall had windows it would use $80\cdot20=1600$ bricks. Each meter of window-free wall adds $40$ bricks, and we have $2120-1600=520$ extra, so $\frac{520}{40}=13$ meters.

**Answer: 13 meters**

rmt-2009-gen-11.title: Two equations
rmt-2009-gen-11.body:
Let the factory normally make $x$ three-button and $y$ five-button mice: $3x+5y=207$ and $5x+3y=281$. Adding: $8(x+y)=488$, so $x+y=61$; subtracting: $2(x-y)=74$, $x-y=37$. Hence $x=49$, $y=12$ (check: $147+60=207$).

**Answer: 49**

rmt-2009-gen-12.title: Difference of squares
rmt-2009-gen-12.body:
$3599=3600-1=60^2-1^2=59\cdot61$, and both $59$ and $61$ are prime. The largest prime factor is $61$.

**Answer: 61**

rmt-2009-gen-13.title: Prime factorisation
rmt-2009-gen-13.body:
$12345=3\cdot5\cdot823$, and $823$ is prime (it is not divisible by any prime up to $28$). The number of divisors is $2\cdot2\cdot2=8$.

**Answer: 8**

rmt-2009-gen-14.title: Worst case
rmt-2009-gen-14.body:
The $26$ gloves form $4+6+3=13$ matching pairs (a left and a right glove each). In the worst case you pull one glove from each pair, $13$ gloves with no match. The $14$th glove must match one of them.

**Answer: 14**

rmt-2009-gen-15.title: Independence
rmt-2009-gen-15.body:
Coin flips are independent, so the first $19$ flips do not matter: the last flip is heads with probability $\frac12$.

**Answer: $\frac12$**

rmt-2009-gen-16.title: Add the rates
rmt-2009-gen-16.body:
Together they prove $\frac16+\frac15=\frac{11}{30}$ theorems per hour, so $100$ theorems take $\frac{100\cdot30}{11}=272.7\ldots\approx273$ hours.

**Answer: 273 hours**

rmt-2009-gen-17.title: Compare the requirements
rmt-2009-gen-17.body:
With $N$ Silly members, the total is $N+25$ and the Sensible votes needed are the least integer $s\ge0$ with $N+s\ge\frac23(N+25)$, i.e. $s\ge\frac{50-N}3$. After expelling one Silly member the requirement is $s'\ge\frac{51-N}3\ge\frac{50-N}3$. So the number of Sensible votes needed never decreases (it can stay the same or go up). Hence there are $0$ such values of $N$.

**Answer: 0**

rmt-2009-gen-17.title: Intuition
rmt-2009-gen-17.body:
Expelling a Silly member removes one guaranteed yes vote but lowers the required count by only $\frac23$ of a vote. So the shortfall that the Sensible party must make up can only grow or stay the same.

**Answer: 0**

rmt-2009-gen-18.title: Factor
rmt-2009-gen-18.body:
$x=1$ is a root, and the polynomial factors as $(x-1)^2(x^2-x+1)$. The quadratic has discriminant $1-4<0$, so the only distinct real root is $x=1$; the sum is $1$.

**Answer: 1**

rmt-2009-gen-18.title: Palindromic polynomial
rmt-2009-gen-18.body:
Divide by $x^2$ and put $u=x+\frac1x$: $x^2+\frac1{x^2}-3\left(x+\frac1x\right)+4=u^2-3u+2=0$, so $u=1$ or $u=2$. $x+\frac1x=2$ gives $x=1$; $x+\frac1x=1$ has no real solution. So the sum of distinct real roots is $1$.

**Answer: 1**

rmt-2009-gen-19.title: Gauss pairing
rmt-2009-gen-19.body:
Pair $k$ with $1000001-k$: there are $500000$ pairs each summing to $1000001$, so the sum is $500000\cdot1000001=500000500000$.

**Answer: 500000500000**

rmt-2009-gen-20.title: Angle sum
rmt-2009-gen-20.body:
A $7$-gon has interior angle sum $5\cdot180^\circ=900^\circ$. The $n$ triangles have angles adding to $180^\circ n$, and the angles at the corners of the polygon are all made up of triangle angles, so $180n\ge900$, i.e. $n\ge5$.

Five triangles suffice: take a regular hexagon made of $6$ triangles around a centre and remove one triangle. The hexagon's $6$ sides lose one side and gain the $2$ edges next to the removed triangle, giving $5+2=7$ sides.

**Answer: 5**

rmt-2009-gen-21.title: Focal distance
rmt-2009-gen-21.body:
For an ellipse with semi-axes $a=2$ and $b=1$ the foci are at distance $c=\sqrt{a^2-b^2}=\sqrt3$ from the centre, so they are $2c=2\sqrt3$ apart.

**Answer: $2\sqrt3$**

rmt-2009-gen-22.title: Factor the expression
rmt-2009-gen-22.body:
$n^4+n^2+1=(n^2+n+1)(n^2-n+1)$. For $n\ge2$ both factors exceed $1$ ($n^2-n+1\ge3$), so the number is composite. For $n=1$ it equals $3$, which is prime. So $n=1$ is the only solution.

**Answer: $n=1$**

rmt-2009-gen-23.title: Each coin independently
rmt-2009-gen-23.body:
A given coin is eaten unless it lands heads on both flips, so it is eaten with probability $1-\frac14=\frac34$, independently of the others. The number eaten is binomial: $P(\ge3)=\binom43\left(\frac34\right)^3\frac14+\left(\frac34\right)^4=\frac{108+81}{256}=\frac{189}{256}$.

**Answer: $\frac{189}{256}$**

rmt-2009-gen-24.title: Rates in area
rmt-2009-gen-24.body:
A $2$ m pizza has area $\pi$, so the three eat $\pi$, $\frac\pi2$, $\frac\pi3$ square meters per minute, together $\frac{11\pi}6$. A pizza of diameter $6$ has area $9\pi$, which takes $\frac{9\pi}{11\pi/6}=\frac{54}{11}$ minutes.

**Answer: $\frac{54}{11}$ minutes**

rmt-2009-gen-25.title: Count factors of 5
rmt-2009-gen-25.body:
$8!=40320$, so we want the number of trailing zeros of $40320!$, i.e. the exponent of $5$ in it (there are plenty of $2$s): $\left\lfloor\frac{40320}5\right\rfloor+\left\lfloor\frac{40320}{25}\right\rfloor+\left\lfloor\frac{40320}{125}\right\rfloor+\left\lfloor\frac{40320}{625}\right\rfloor+\left\lfloor\frac{40320}{3125}\right\rfloor+\left\lfloor\frac{40320}{15625}\right\rfloor=8064+1612+322+64+12+2=10076$.

**Answer: 10076**
